entities.summary: Venutius was a 1st-century king of the Brigantes in northern Britain, whose reign was marked by the Roman conquest. He is believed to have been the leader of the Brigantes during the time of Emperor Hadrian's visit to Britain in 122 CE, and it is possible that he may have been the king who was deposed and replaced by the Roman governor Quintus Petillius Cerialis in 122 CE. The Roman historian Tacitus wrote about Venutius in his book 'Agricola', where he described him as a fierce warrior who was known for his bravery and military prowess. Venutius' legacy is still remembered today as a symbol of British resistance against Roman rule, and he is often celebrated in Scottish folklore as a champion of Scottish independence. Despite his significance, Venutius is still a relatively unknown figure, and more research is needed to fully understand his life and reign.
